key_insight: SymFT speeds up fault-tolerant quantum circuit simulation by symbolically separating Clifford/Pauli frames from the probabilistic parts that actually affect sampling, while compactly tracking only active non-stabilizer degrees of freedom.
engineering_relevance: This makes large stabilizer-heavy and near-Clifford workloads—such as surface-code, magic-state cultivation, and distillation circuits—practical to simulate much faster on CPU.
method: Symbolic Clifford–Pauli frame factorization: keep Clifford and Pauli frames symbolic so only Pauli rotations, measurements, noise, and feedback drive branch probabilities.
Adaptive stabilizer-coordinate planning: use a shared tableau to choose a basis once, then store only active non-stabilizer coordinates in a dense vector.
Direct multi-coordinate sampling: avoid per-shot tableau updates and repeated localization-induced Clifford transformations of the dense state representation.
evidence_signal: On a single CPU core, SymFT is reported to be 2.51–2.56× faster than Stim on surface-code circuits, 1.86–3.51× faster than Clifft on magic-state cultivation/distillation circuits, and over 100× faster than the authors’ prior SOFT simulator on tested cultivation circuits.
watch_item: The approach appears optimized for Clifford-dominated and near-Clifford workloads, so performance and implementation complexity may be less favorable when circuits have many strongly non-stabilizer operations or frequent basis changes.
paper_title: SymFT: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuit Simulation via Symbolic Clifford--Pauli Frames and Stabilizer Coordinates
